title: Three ways to compose an atmosphere
question: All three use an open canvas with no nodes or wiring, evocative artwork, 3–6 sound layers, and contextual settings. They differ in what the canvas is organized around. Expand a study to see its full visual treatment; the small previews simplify the controls.

options.label: Scene atlas
options.thesis: Prepare a scene as a landscape of moods, opening one composition without losing its neighbors.
options.viewport: Tavern Evening is the open composition with five loosely arranged sound tiles; Rain Rolls In and Last Call remain smaller mood landmarks elsewhere on the canvas; the selected sound’s settings live at right.
options.risk: The richest scene context, but also the most to understand: mood membership and the current editing focus must stay unmistakable.

options.label: Inside the atmosphere
options.thesis: Work inside one mood’s artwork, arranging its sounds across an immersive but legible stage.
options.viewport: A narrow mood navigator at left, the tavern artwork filling the central canvas, and five small sound tiles placed around its open center; selecting a sound reveals settings at right; listening and saving stay anchored below.
options.risk: The most immediate atmosphere, but artwork must never compete with sound names or turn the editor into wallpaper with controls on top.

options.label: Around a mood
options.thesis: Make the atmosphere the centerpiece, with its sounds gathered around it like ingredients in a composition.
options.viewport: A large illustrated Tavern Evening portrait anchors the canvas, with five arrangeable sound tiles around it and no connecting lines; selected-sound settings open in a shallow bottom dock rather than taking a side column.
options.risk: A clearer one-mood focus, but the initial arrangement must feel like a helpful starting point rather than a fixed diagram.
